quick_skim.title: Finding Fast Filters
quick_skim.abstract: Processing images, video, and audio often requires running large finite impulse response (FIR) filters with strict performance and latency requirements. Prior methods for fast filter approximations are special cases or combinations of a few key techniques: multi-rate and recurrent filtering, and decomposing filters into sums or cascades. We unify these techniques as primitives within a single design language for fast 1D and 2D filters. Given a target filter to approximate, we automatically search this program space, fitting continuous parameters with gradient descent, to generate a Pareto frontier of algorithms that trade off performance with quality. Our system produces substantially higher-quality and faster filter approximations than have been previously described for several popular imaging and audio filters. Furthermore we demonstrate how to automatically lower programs in this design space to optimized, vectorized, parallel, C++ code which is fused for data locality.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Proposes a design language for fast FIR filter approximations using gradient descent to search the program space, generating Pareto-optimal algorithms for imaging and audio.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 论文针对图像和音频处理中大规模FIR滤波器的性能与延迟需求，提出一种统一的快速滤波器设计语言。通过将多速率滤波、递归滤波等机制作为原语，并利用梯度下降自动搜索程序空间，生成性能与质量帕累托前沿的算法。实验表明，该方法在多个流行图像和音频滤波任务上取得了更高质量和更快速度的滤波器近似。
